I am analyzing the `prefetch_related` implementation and descriptor methods to trace how deferred fields and cached instances interact during nested prefetches.
I have resolved the issue where nested `Prefetch` lookups following relations back to a parent object had their cached instances overwritten by the outer `get_prefetch_queryset()` call.

### Cause
When evaluating `queryset` inside `get_prefetch_queryset()` on [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-eewrebrb/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L120-L150), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-eewrebrb/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L365-L382), and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`'s [`RelatedManager`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-eewrebrb/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L634-L654), any nested prefetches (or `select_related()` lookups) on `queryset` are executed during iteration and populate the reverse relation cache on each `rel_obj`. However, the loop in `get_prefetch_queryset()` unconditionally set the reverse relation cache on `rel_obj` to the parent `instance` from `instances_dict`, overwriting the already cached object from the inner prefetch.

### Solution
Updated `get_prefetch_queryset()` in [`related_descriptors.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-eewrebrb/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py) to check whether the relation is already cached on `rel_obj` (`is_cached(rel_obj)`) before caching `instance`.
